quests.hint: This verb means to make a formal written record or official document of something.
quests.explanation: 'Document evidence,' 'well-documented,' and 'document your findings' are key. 'Documentation' is the noun. 'Documented' as an adjective means officially recorded and verified.
quests.textToSpeak: It is essential to ___ every decision made during the research process for future reference.
quests.correctAnswer: It is essential to document every decision made during the research process for future reference.

quests.hint: This verb means to officially put on record that you oppose or object to something.
quests.explanation: 'Lodge a protest,' 'lodge a complaint,' and 'lodge an objection' are key. 'Lodge' implies formal submission. 'Lodge with the court' means to file officially with a legal body.
quests.textToSpeak: Three board members asked to ___ their objection to the vote in the official minutes.
quests.correctAnswer: Three board members asked to lodge their objection to the vote in the official minutes.

quests.hint: This verb means to seek or ask for something formally and officially.
quests.explanation: 'Solicit feedback,' 'solicit applications,' and 'solicit support' are key. 'Solicitation' is the noun. 'Soliciting' can also mean asking for money in public. 'Solicitor' is a British legal term.
quests.textToSpeak: The committee decided to ___ written responses from all major stakeholders before deciding.
quests.correctAnswer: The committee decided to solicit written responses from all major stakeholders before deciding.

quests.hint: This verb means to officially begin or start a formal legal or institutional process.
quests.explanation: 'Initiate proceedings,' 'initiate a review,' and 'initiate contact' are key. 'Initiative' is related. 'Initial' (adjective) means first. 'Initiation' is the noun for the start of a process.
quests.textToSpeak: The regulator has the power to ___ formal proceedings against any company it suspects.
quests.correctAnswer: The regulator has the power to initiate formal proceedings against any company it suspects.

quests.hint: This verb means to formally make known or announce in an authoritative way.
quests.explanation: 'Declare an emergency,' 'declare war,' and 'declare independence' are key. 'Declaration' is the noun. 'Declare' implies a formal, official, and usually significant announcement.
quests.textToSpeak: The World Health Organization formally ___ a global public health emergency in early January.
quests.correctAnswer: The World Health Organization formally declared a global public health emergency in early January.

quests.hint: This verb means to formally bring a legal case or criminal charges against someone.
quests.explanation: 'Institute proceedings,' 'institute a claim,' and 'institute an inquiry' are key. More formal than 'begin' or 'start.' 'Institution' (noun) means both an organization and the act of starting something.
quests.textToSpeak: The company decided to ___ legal proceedings against its former partner for breach of contract.
quests.correctAnswer: The company decided to institute legal proceedings against its former partner for breach of contract.

quests.hint: This verb means to make a strong formal objection to a decision or claim.
quests.explanation: 'Contest a will,' 'contest the result,' and 'vigorously contest' are key. 'Contestation' is the noun. 'Contested' as an adjective means disputed: 'a contested election.'
quests.textToSpeak: The family decided to ___ the will on the grounds that the deceased lacked mental capacity.
quests.correctAnswer: The family decided to contest the will on the grounds that the deceased lacked mental capacity.

quests.hint: This verb means to formally object to or express opposition against something.
quests.explanation: 'Oppose a motion,' 'strongly oppose,' and 'opposition to' are key. 'Opposition' is the noun. The 'opposition party' in a parliament challenges the ruling government.
quests.textToSpeak: Three council members publicly ___ the plan to build on protected green-belt land.
quests.correctAnswer: Three council members publicly opposed the plan to build on protected green-belt land.

quests.hint: This verb means to formally appeal to a higher body or authority to reconsider a decision.
quests.explanation: 'Refer to a higher court,' 'refer the matter,' and 'refer to arbitration' are key. 'Referral' is the noun. 'Referred' as an adjective: 'a referred case' goes to a specialist.
quests.textToSpeak: The disputed decision was ___ to the Supreme Court for a definitive ruling.
quests.correctAnswer: The disputed decision was referred to the Supreme Court for a definitive ruling.

quests.hint: This noun refers to the power or authority to take an action in a given situation.
quests.explanation: 'Locus standi,' 'standing in law,' and 'lack of standing' are key. 'Standing' in law means the legal right to bring a case. 'Long-standing' means established for a long time.
quests.textToSpeak: The environmental group was denied ___ to bring the case because it was not directly affected.
quests.correctAnswer: The environmental group was denied standing to bring the case because it was not directly affected.

quests.hint: This noun refers to the power to make final decisions and override others in a system.
quests.explanation: 'Ultimate authority,' 'sovereign authority,' and 'exercise authority' are key. 'Sovereignty' is a related term. 'Authority' can mean power, a body with power, or expertise.
quests.textToSpeak: The constitution vests ___ authority in the parliament rather than in the executive branch.
quests.correctAnswer: The constitution vests ultimate authority in the parliament rather than in the executive branch.

quests.hint: This noun refers to the official power or right to make decisions and enforce rules.
quests.explanation: 'Claim authority,' 'exercise authority,' and 'have authority over' are key. 'Authoritative' is the adjective. 'Authorities' (plural) often refers to government bodies.
quests.textToSpeak: The international tribunal claimed ___ over all crimes committed within the conflict zone.
quests.correctAnswer: The international tribunal claimed authority over all crimes committed within the conflict zone.

quests.hint: This verb means to officially and publicly state that something is wrong or unacceptable.
quests.explanation: 'Condemn an action,' 'strongly condemned,' and 'international condemnation' are key. 'Condemnation' is the noun. Stronger than 'criticise' - it implies a formal moral judgment.
quests.textToSpeak: The UN Security Council voted unanimously to ___ the attack as a violation of international law.
quests.correctAnswer: The UN Security Council voted unanimously to condemn the attack as a violation of international law.

quests.hint: This verb means to formally and officially cancel or reverse a decision or judgment.
quests.explanation: 'Overturn a conviction,' 'overturn a ruling,' and 'overturned on appeal' are key. 'Overturn' implies a complete reversal. 'Overturn precedent' means to change an established legal standard.
quests.textToSpeak: The appeals court ___ the original verdict, finding that the trial had been fundamentally flawed.
quests.correctAnswer: The appeals court overturned the original verdict, finding that the trial had been fundamentally flawed.

quests.hint: This verb means to approve, give permission, or officially allow something to proceed.
quests.explanation: 'Sanction an action,' 'officially sanctioned,' and 'require sanction' are key. 'Sanction' also means a penalty (noun): 'economic sanctions.' Both meanings are common and important.
quests.textToSpeak: The board must formally ___ any expenditure over fifty thousand pounds.
quests.correctAnswer: The board must formally sanction any expenditure over fifty thousand pounds.

quests.hint: This noun refers to an act or statement that shows particular respect for an achievement.
quests.explanation: 'Pay tribute to,' 'a tribute to,' and 'glowing tribute' are key. 'Tribute' can also be a regular payment made to show submission: 'pay tribute to a ruler.'
quests.textToSpeak: The president paid a generous ___ to the scientists whose work had saved millions of lives.
quests.correctAnswer: The president paid a generous tribute to the scientists whose work had saved millions of lives.

quests.hint: This noun refers to the process by which one generation passes its culture to the next.
quests.explanation: 'Cultural transmission,' 'transmission of knowledge,' and 'intergenerational transmission' are key. Also used in disease ('disease transmission') and broadcasting ('signal transmission').
quests.textToSpeak: The oral ___ of traditional knowledge is threatened as fewer young people speak the language.
quests.correctAnswer: The oral transmission of traditional knowledge is threatened as fewer young people speak the language.

quests.hint: This noun refers to the quality of being completely trustworthy and reliable over time.
quests.explanation: 'Credibility of a source,' 'undermine credibility,' and 'establish credibility' are key. 'Credible' is the adjective. 'Lack of credibility' destroys trust. 'Credibility gap' is the difference between claim and reality.
quests.textToSpeak: Years of consistent, accurate reporting had earned the outlet enormous ___ with its audience.
quests.correctAnswer: Years of consistent, accurate reporting had earned the outlet enormous credibility with its audience.

quests.hint: This verb means to officially suspend or interrupt something temporarily.
quests.explanation: 'Suspend a sentence,' 'suspend a licence,' and 'suspend a member' are key. 'Suspension' is the noun. 'Suspended sentence' in law means a punishment delayed on condition of good behaviour.
quests.textToSpeak: The regulator decided to ___ the company's trading licence pending a full investigation.
quests.correctAnswer: The regulator decided to suspend the company's trading licence pending a full investigation.

quests.hint: This verb means to maintain something in its current condition or protect it from deterioration.
quests.explanation: 'Preserve evidence,' 'preserve a tradition,' and 'preservation order' are key. 'Preservation' is the noun. 'Self-preservation' is the instinct to protect yourself. 'Well-preserved' means still in good condition.
quests.textToSpeak: The court ordered that all digital communications be ___ until the investigation was complete.
quests.correctAnswer: The court ordered that all digital communications be preserved until the investigation was complete.

quests.hint: This verb means to officially remove someone from a position of power or authority.
quests.explanation: 'Depose a ruler,' 'deposed in a coup,' and 'deposition' are key. 'Deposition' (noun) also means sworn testimony. 'Depose a witness' means to take their statement under oath.
quests.textToSpeak: The military ___ the elected president in an overnight coup met with international condemnation.
quests.correctAnswer: The military deposed the elected president in an overnight coup met with international condemnation.

quests.hint: This noun refers to the state of being complete and self-sufficient without external support.
quests.explanation: 'Financial self-sufficiency,' 'energy self-sufficiency,' and 'strive for self-sufficiency' are key. 'Self-sufficient' is the adjective. 'Autarky' is the economic policy of national self-sufficiency.
quests.textToSpeak: The community aims to achieve ___ in food production within the next five years.
quests.correctAnswer: The community aims to achieve self-sufficiency in food production within the next five years.

quests.hint: This noun refers to agreement or correspondence between different positions, especially political views.
quests.explanation: 'Political alignment,' 'align with,' and 'strategic alignment' are key. 'Align' is the verb. 'Misalignment' means a lack of correspondence between things that should match.
quests.textToSpeak: There is growing ___ between the two parties' positions on tax and public spending.
quests.correctAnswer: There is growing alignment between the two parties' positions on tax and public spending.

quests.hint: This noun refers to the quality of being completely truthful, even about things that may be uncomfortable.
quests.explanation: 'Radical candour,' 'speak with candour,' and 'the candour of her account' are key. 'Candid' is the adjective: 'a candid interview.' 'In all candour' means honestly and frankly.
quests.textToSpeak: She spoke with remarkable ___ about the failures of the policy she had helped to design.
quests.correctAnswer: She spoke with remarkable candour about the failures of the policy she had helped to design.

quests.hint: This noun refers to information or evidence that is directly relevant to the point being made.
quests.explanation: 'Pertinence of the evidence,' 'the pertinence of' and 'of great pertinence' are key. 'Pertinent' is the adjective: 'a pertinent point.' More formal than 'relevance' in academic usage.
quests.textToSpeak: The judge questioned the ___ of the witness's account to the specific charge before the court.
quests.correctAnswer: The judge questioned the pertinence of the witness's account to the specific charge before the court.

quests.hint: This noun refers to a key piece of information or critical point in a case or argument.
quests.explanation: 'The crux of the matter,' 'the crux of the argument,' and 'at the crux of' are key. 'Crux' is the most essential point. 'Nub' is a synonym. 'At the crux' means at the heart of the issue.
quests.textToSpeak: The ___ of the dispute is whether the original agreement was legally binding at the time.
quests.correctAnswer: The crux of the dispute is whether the original agreement was legally binding at the time.

quests.hint: This noun refers to the specific aspect or detail that is central to understanding a problem.
quests.explanation: 'The nub of the issue,' 'get to the nub,' and 'the very nub of the matter' are key. 'Nub' means the central point or core difficulty. Similar to 'crux' but slightly more informal.
quests.textToSpeak: The ___ of the problem is that the data does not support the assumptions the model relies on.
quests.correctAnswer: The nub of the problem is that the data does not support the assumptions the model relies on.

quests.hint: This noun refers to a prediction or judgement about the likely future of a situation.
quests.explanation: 'A positive prognosis,' 'a grim prognosis,' and 'the economic prognosis' are key. Originally a medical term for the expected course of a disease. Now used broadly for any forecast.
quests.textToSpeak: The economic ___ for the region remains uncertain given the volatility of global markets.
quests.correctAnswer: The economic prognosis for the region remains uncertain given the volatility of global markets.

quests.hint: This noun refers to a condition that must be met before something else can happen.
quests.explanation: 'A precondition for,' 'set preconditions,' and 'without preconditions' are key. 'Precondition' is stronger than 'condition' - it must be met before talks or agreements can begin.
quests.textToSpeak: The union insisted that meaningful wage increases were a ___ for any return to work.
quests.correctAnswer: The union insisted that meaningful wage increases were a precondition for any return to work.

quests.hint: This noun refers to the likely or natural result that flows from a set of circumstances.
quests.explanation: 'A logical corollary,' 'a direct corollary,' and 'by corollary' are key. A 'corollary' follows logically from something proved. Used in mathematics and philosophy.
quests.textToSpeak: Greater transparency is a necessary ___ of any genuine commitment to democratic accountability.
quests.correctAnswer: Greater transparency is a necessary corollary of any genuine commitment to democratic accountability.
